% The NAIVE conversion: class swapped, the bare [b] frame option left alone.
% This is the defect C-FRAME-OPT is about. ltx-talk takes a key-value list, so a
% list of nothing but bare words is discarded whole -- no error, no warning, right
% page count, identical extracted text. The frame just renders centred.
%
% Measured (lualatex, pdftotext -bbox yMin of the word "paragraph" as a fraction
% of page height; 0.0 is the top edge):
%   before.tex  0.950  beamer [b]                    -- bottom
%   after.tex   0.868  vertical-alignment=bottom     -- bottom
%   naive.tex   0.475  bare [b], discarded           -- CENTRED
%
% The fractions differ between the first two because beamer 16:9 is 272.126pt tall
% and ltx-talk 283.465pt; both are unambiguously bottom-aligned, and the naive one
% is unambiguously not.
%
% If assert-naive.sh ever fails, ltx-talk has started parsing option lists without
% an "=", or errors on an unknown bare word. Either is the entry's revisit-when.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[b]
\frametitle{Pinned to the bottom}
This paragraph sits at the foot of the slide, under the empty space.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
